definitions.active_repos: Repositories that are not archived, not forks, and pushed_at within 365 days.
definitions.critical_repos: Repositories whose custom property criticality/tier is in (critical, high, tier-0, tier-1); if no such property exists, the 20 most recently pushed active repositories, plus any repository with a production-like environment.
definitions.eligible_repos: Active repositories to which a feature can apply (e.g. code scanning: >= 1 CodeQL-supported language; Dependabot: >= 1 supported manifest / SBOM returns packages).
definitions.sample_cap: Repository-level collectors run on all active repositories up to 300; beyond that, a stratified sample by visibility and primary language is drawn and documented in evidence/org/{org}/sample.json.
definitions.third_party_action: A uses: reference whose owner is not the customer's organization, not 'actions', not 'github' and not a local path.
definitions.origin: Framework checklist = control wording from the published GitHub Well-Architected pillar checklists; Security deep dive = control grounded on GitHub Docs that supplements the checklist (identity and access, repository governance, CI/CD and supply chain, GitHub Advanced Security, Copilot security governance, audit/monitoring/incident readiness, Secure SDLC alignment).

automation_levels.Full: The agent computes the metrics and proposes IMPLEMENTED / PARTIAL / NOT_IMPLEMENTED from data alone; the assessor may override.
automation_levels.Partial: The agent computes the metrics and proposes a state flagged 'confirm'; the interview question must be answered before the state is final.
automation_levels.Manual: No environment query; the agent exports the interview question / document request and the assessor rates the control.

collectors.endpoint: query { repository(owner:$o,name:$r){ pullRequests(last:100,states:[MERGED],orderBy:{field:UPDATED_AT,direction:DESC}){ totalCount nodes{ number createdAt mergedAt additions deletions changedFiles author{ login __typename } reviewDecision reviews(first:50){ totalCount nodes{ state submittedAt author{ login } } } comments{ totalCount } commits{ totalCount } closingIssuesReferences(first:1){ totalCount } labels(first:10){ nodes{ name } } } } } }

controls.control: Document all current manual processes.
controls.rule: IMPL if a written inventory of manual processes (release, approvals, environment setup, access requests) exists and was reviewed in the last 12 months; PART if it exists but is older than 12 months or covers only some teams; NOT if no inventory.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Show us the current list of manual steps in your delivery process (release, approvals, environment provisioning, access). Who owns it and when was it last updated?

controls.control: Identify repetitive, time-consuming, and error-prone tasks.
controls.rule: IMPL if repetitive/error-prone tasks are identified with frequency and time cost per task; PART if identified qualitatively only; NOT if not identified.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which repetitive, time-consuming or error-prone tasks have you identified, and do you know how much time each costs per week?

controls.control: Involve key stakeholders to gain insights and perspectives on the needs of the organization and any frictions to resolve.
controls.rule: IMPL if impact (time, defects, delay) is quantified for the identified manual tasks; PART if impact is estimated for some; NOT if not assessed.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How do you measure the impact of manual work on delivery speed and quality? Show an example.

controls.control: Assess the scalability and future growth potential of automation solutions.
controls.rule: IMPL if candidate tasks have a documented feasibility/priority assessment (effort vs benefit); PART if discussed but not documented; NOT otherwise.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Is there an automation backlog with feasibility and priority per item? Who decides what gets automated next?

controls.control: Prioritize processes based on pain points and inefficiencies.
controls.rule: IMPL if each candidate has an expected benefit (hours saved, defects avoided) and the top items are scheduled; PART if benefits are stated without scheduling; NOT otherwise.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: For the top automation candidates, what benefit do you expect and when are they planned?

controls.control: Foster a culture of automation within the organization.
controls.rule: Compute actions_adoption = active repos with >= 1 active workflow / active repos. IMPL if >= 80% and Actions usage metrics show runs in the last 30 days for >= 70% of those repos; PART if 40-80%; NOT if < 40%. Interview confirms leadership sponsorship and an automation community/guild.
controls.interview_question: Who sponsors automation in engineering leadership, and is there a community (guild, channel, inner-source repo) where teams share workflows?

controls.control: Incorporate automation concepts into documentation and processes.
controls.rule: IMPL if the organization .github repository (or a platform docs repo) contains workflow templates (workflow-templates/*.yml with *.properties.json) AND >= 70% of active repos have a README or docs/ describing how CI/CD runs (README mentions 'workflow', 'pipeline', 'CI' or links to .github/workflows); PART if templates exist OR docs coverage 40-70%; NOT if neither.
controls.interview_question: Where do developers read how automation works in your organization (onboarding docs, engineering handbook, starter workflows)?

controls.control: Automate repetitive tasks and integrate CI/CD pipelines.
controls.rule: Per active repo: has_ci = a workflow triggered on pull_request or push with a build/test job; has_cd = a workflow with environment: or a deployment event or a deploy-named job. IMPL if >= 80% of active repos have CI and >= 50% of repos with releases/deployments have CD via Actions (or a documented external CD tool integrated by webhook/App); PART if CI 50-80%; NOT if CI < 50%.

controls.control: Implement GitHub Actions using GitHub-hosted runners for CI/CD.
controls.rule: Classify runs-on values across all workflows: github_hosted (ubuntu-*/windows-*/macos-* or hosted-runner labels) vs self_hosted. IMPL if >= 1 workflow per active repo uses GitHub-hosted (or larger hosted) runners for CI and self-hosted runners are used only for documented needs (interview optional); PART if 50-80% of CI runs are on hosted runners; NOT if Actions CI is absent or entirely on unmanaged self-hosted runners without runner groups.

controls.control: Provide learning sessions on automated workflows and security features.
controls.rule: Data: security feature coverage (dependabot alerts, code scanning default setup, secret scanning) from configurations. IMPL if a training/enablement programme on workflows and security features exists (sessions in the last 12 months with attendance records) AND coverage >= 80%; PART if either exists; NOT if neither.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: What training or enablement have developers received on GitHub Actions and the security features (Dependabot, code scanning, secret scanning) in the last 12 months?

controls.control: Evaluate the benefits of automation against cost and maintenance.
controls.rule: Data: Actions minutes used (billing), minutes by runner OS, self-hosted runner count, hosted larger runner usage. IMPL if a cost/benefit review of automation (minutes, runner infrastructure, maintenance effort) is done at least quarterly with a named owner; PART if costs are visible but not reviewed; NOT if not tracked.
controls.interview_question: Who reviews Actions consumption (minutes, larger runners, self-hosted infrastructure) and maintenance effort, and how often?

controls.control: Establish a strategy for platform automation adoption.
controls.rule: IMPL if a written automation strategy/roadmap exists (owner, targets, timeline) AND platform conventions are visible in the environment (reusable workflows in a shared repo referenced by >= 30% of active repos OR required workflows in rulesets); PART if either; NOT if neither.
controls.interview_question: Is there an automation strategy or platform roadmap? Who owns it and what are the targets for the next 12 months?

controls.control: Leverage GitHub Enterprise features like Actions, Packages, Code Scanning, Secret Scanning, and Dependabot.
controls.rule: Compute per feature: actions_pct (active repos with workflows), packages_used (org packages count > 0), code_scanning_pct, secret_scanning_pct, dependabot_pct (security_and_analysis / configurations). IMPL if actions >= 80% and each of code scanning, secret scanning and Dependabot >= 80% of eligible active repos; PART if actions >= 50% and >= 2 security features >= 50%; NOT otherwise.

controls.control: Develop automated workflows for notifications and updates.
controls.rule: IMPL if notification automation exists: workflows using a Slack/Teams notification action (slackapi/slack-github-action, 8398a7/action-slack, Teams webhook steps) OR the Slack/Microsoft Teams GitHub App is installed, AND scheduled workflows (on: schedule) or Dependabot handle updates in >= 30% of active repos; PART if only one of the two; NOT if none.

controls.control: Establish and enforce code implementation and deployment standards.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 80% of active repos have an effective default-branch rule requiring pull requests AND required status checks (or a required workflow) enforced by rulesets/branch protection; PART if 50-80%; NOT if < 50%.

controls.control: Continuously monitor and optimize automated workflows.
controls.rule: Data: 90-day CI success rate, median duration, median queue time, failure trend. IMPL if success rate >= 90%, median queue time < 2 min, and the customer reviews Actions performance metrics at least monthly (interview); PART if metrics are acceptable but not reviewed, or reviewed with success rate 75-90%; NOT if success rate < 75% and no review.
controls.interview_question: Who looks at workflow failure rates, duration and queue times, and how often? What was the last optimisation made?

controls.control: Regularly review and optimize GitHub Enterprise automation configurations.
controls.rule: Data: Actions policies (allowed actions, workflow permissions), runner groups and runner inventory with last-seen status. IMPL if a periodic (at least semi-annual) review of Actions configuration is evidenced (change tickets, review notes) and no offline runners older than 30 days remain; PART if reviews happen ad hoc; NOT if never reviewed.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: When did you last review the organization Actions policies, runner groups and runner fleet? Show the record.

controls.control: Define clear standards and guidelines for platform integration.
controls.rule: IMPL if an integration standard exists (authentication method: GitHub App preferred over PAT, webhook secrets, rate-limit handling, ownership) reviewed in 12 months; PART if partial guidance; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Do you have a written standard for integrating with GitHub (GitHub Apps vs tokens, webhook secrets, ownership)? Show it.

controls.control: Ensure compatibility and scalability across different systems.
controls.rule: IMPL if integration requests follow a defined process with an approver and a registry; PART if informal; NOT if uncontrolled.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How does a team request a new integration or GitHub App today? Who approves it?

controls.control: Identify individuals or teams responsible for driving integration.
controls.rule: IMPL if a named owner/board governs integrations and reviews them at least annually; PART if ownership exists without review; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who owns the integration landscape (Apps, OAuth apps, webhooks) and when was it last reviewed?

controls.control: Develop and enforce consistent policies, standards, and best practices.
controls.rule: IMPL if integrations are evaluated against security and cost criteria before approval; PART if evaluated informally; NOT if not evaluated.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: What criteria (security review, data access, cost) are applied before an integration is approved?

controls.control: Create comprehensive integration process documentation for developers.
controls.rule: IMPL if each production integration has documentation (purpose, owner, auth method, data flows, runbook) that matches the installed inventory; PART if >= 50% documented; NOT if < 50%.
controls.interview_question: Show the documentation for your GitHub integrations: purpose, owner, credentials used, failure handling.

controls.control: Ensure consistency and standardization in integration practices.
controls.rule: IMPL if each production integration has documentation (purpose, owner, auth method, data flows, runbook) that matches the installed inventory; PART if >= 50% documented; NOT if < 50%.
controls.interview_question: Show the documentation for your GitHub integrations: purpose, owner, credentials used, failure handling.

controls.control: Identify key integration points and evaluate potential solutions.
controls.rule: Build the integration inventory: GitHub Apps (app_slug, permissions, repository_selection), org webhooks (host, events), approved OAuth apps. IMPL if inventory non-empty AND every app maps to a known category (chat, work tracking, CI/CD, security, code quality) or a customer-provided owner; PART if >= 70% mapped; NOT if unmapped or no integrations at all.

controls.control: Prioritize integrations based on organizational needs and goals.
controls.rule: IMPL if the installed apps align with stated priorities (work tracking, chat, CI/CD, security) and no unused apps (updated_at > 365 days and no webhook deliveries) remain; PART if <= 20% unused; NOT if > 20% unused or no prioritisation.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which integrations matter most to your delivery flow, and which installed apps are no longer used?

controls.control: Integrate GitHub Enterprise with other enterprise systems, or look to migrate to GitHub where possible.
controls.rule: IMPL if at least one integration exists in each of: work tracking (Jira / Azure Boards / GitHub Issues+Projects in use), chat (Slack/Teams app), CI/CD or deployment target (Actions with environments or Azure Pipelines/Jenkins app/webhook), and security tooling (code scanning tool or security App); PART if 2-3 categories; NOT if <= 1.

controls.control: Implement advanced monitoring and management tools for integrated systems.
controls.rule: IMPL if every active org webhook has < 5% failed deliveries (status_code >= 400 or status != OK) in the last 100 deliveries AND API insights show rate_limited_request_count == 0 for integrations in the last 7 days; PART if any hook 5-20% failures or rate limiting observed once; NOT if any hook > 20% failures or hooks inactive due to failures.

controls.control: Continuously evaluate and refine integration processes.
controls.rule: IMPL if integration health (webhook failures, app permissions, token expiry) is reviewed at least quarterly with recorded actions; PART if reviewed reactively after incidents; NOT if not reviewed.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How do you find out when an integration breaks (webhook failures, expired tokens)? When was the last review?

controls.control: Use GitHub Enterprise APIs and webhooks for custom integrations.
controls.rule: IMPL if custom integrations authenticate as GitHub Apps (installations with owner != marketplace vendor) or fine-grained PATs with expiry, and webhooks use a secret with insecure_ssl = 0; PART if some custom integrations use classic PATs or webhooks without secrets (<= 30%); NOT if > 30% of hooks lack secrets or classic PATs dominate.

controls.control: Promote a culture of continuous improvement and learning.
controls.rule: IMPL if learning time is explicitly allocated (e.g. >= 4h/month) and leadership promotes it; PART if encouraged without allocation; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Is time for learning explicitly allocated for engineers? How do leaders encourage experimentation?

controls.control: Encourage employees to take ownership of their process skills.
controls.rule: IMPL if learning time is explicitly allocated (e.g. >= 4h/month) and leadership promotes it; PART if encouraged without allocation; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Is time for learning explicitly allocated for engineers? How do leaders encourage experimentation?

controls.control: Offer training sessions on new tools, technologies, and best practices.
controls.rule: IMPL if a catalogue of GitHub learning resources (GitHub Skills, internal courses, certifications) exists and >= 50% of developers completed at least one item in 12 months; PART if resources exist without tracking; NOT if none.

controls.control: Facilitate knowledge sharing and collaboration across teams.
controls.rule: IMPL if a catalogue of GitHub learning resources (GitHub Skills, internal courses, certifications) exists and >= 50% of developers completed at least one item in 12 months; PART if resources exist without tracking; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which GitHub learning resources or certifications are available to developers, and what share used them in the last year?

controls.control: Provide administrative and user training on GitHub Enterprise features and best practices.
controls.rule: IMPL if a catalogue of GitHub learning resources (GitHub Skills, internal courses, certifications) exists and >= 50% of developers completed at least one item in 12 months; PART if resources exist without tracking; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which GitHub learning resources or certifications are available to developers, and what share used them in the last year?

controls.control: Gather user feedback on automated and integrated processes.

controls.control: Use feedback to identify areas for enhancement and optimization.
controls.rule: IMPL if retrospectives or surveys feed a tracked improvement backlog with closed items; PART if feedback is gathered without tracked actions; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)

controls.control: Collect feedback on GitHub Enterprise usage and performance.
controls.rule: IMPL if retrospectives or surveys feed a tracked improvement backlog with closed items; PART if feedback is gathered without tracked actions; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)

controls.control: Continuously update process documentation and tooling.
controls.rule: IMPL if engineering practices are reviewed against new GitHub capabilities at least annually (changelog review, roadmap sessions) with adopted changes recorded; PART if ad hoc; NOT if never.

controls.control: Stay informed about emerging technologies and integration platforms.

controls.rule: IMPL if fine-grained PATs require approval, classic PATs are restricted, maximum lifetime <= 366 days (fine-grained) and custom integrations use GitHub Apps; PART if approval required but classic allowed, or lifetime unlimited; NOT if tokens unrestricted.

controls.control: Monitor API usage for anomalies.
controls.rule: IMPL if API insights are available and no actor has rate_limited_request_count > 0 in the last 7 days, and PAT/OAuth events are streamed to the SIEM; PART if insights reviewed but rate limiting present; NOT if API usage is not visible (GHES: N/A for insights; rely on audit log).

controls.control: Establish proper best practice guidelines for API usage, including token usage.
controls.rule: IMPL if API/token guidance exists (prefer Apps, fine-grained scopes, expiry, storage, no tokens in code) and is referenced by the integration standard; PART if partial; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Do you have written guidance on API and token usage for developers and integrators?

controls.control: Set up monitoring and alerting for unusual activities within GitHub Enterprise.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log streaming is active and >= 5 GitHub detections exist in the SIEM with routing to on-call; PART if streaming with < 5 detections; NOT if no streaming.

controls.control: Regularly review and update monitoring rules and audit logs.
controls.rule: IMPL if detection rules and audit log usage are reviewed quarterly with a change log; PART if annually; NOT if never.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: When were GitHub detection rules last tuned, and by whom?

controls.control: Ensure alerts are actionable and promptly addressed.
controls.rule: IMPL if GitHub alerts have an owner, a runbook link and are closed within SLA (report from the SOC); PART if owned without SLA tracking; NOT if unowned.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Show the SOC's handling record for GitHub-related alerts in the last quarter.

controls.control: Ensure compliance with any data residency requirements, especially when replicating with GitHub Enterprise Server.
controls.rule: IMPL if data residency requirements are documented and the deployment (GHEC region/data residency, GHES location) satisfies them with evidence; PART if requirements known but not evidenced; NOT if unknown.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which data residency requirements apply, and how does your GitHub deployment satisfy them?

controls.control: Regularly review data residency configurations.
controls.rule: IMPL if data residency requirements are documented and the deployment (GHEC region/data residency, GHES location) satisfies them with evidence; PART if requirements known but not evidenced; NOT if unknown.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which data residency requirements apply, and how does your GitHub deployment satisfy them?

controls.control: Document data residency policies and procedures.
controls.rule: IMPL if data residency requirements are documented and the deployment (GHEC region/data residency, GHES location) satisfies them with evidence; PART if requirements known but not evidenced; NOT if unknown.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which data residency requirements apply, and how does your GitHub deployment satisfy them?

controls.control: Review and secure third-party integrations with GitHub Enterprise to prevent potential security risks.
controls.rule: IMPL if OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, every installed GitHub App has an owner and approval record (customer registry), and no app has permissions broader than needed (no 'administration: write' or 'members: write' without justification); PART if restrictions enabled but registry incomplete (< 80%); NOT if restrictions disabled.

controls.control: Regularly assess the security of third-party integrations.
controls.rule: IMPL if third-party integrations are re-assessed at least annually (vendor security, permissions) with records; PART if reviewed only at onboarding; NOT if never.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How often are installed apps and integrations re-assessed for security and necessity?

controls.control: Ensure third-party providers comply with your security standards.
controls.rule: IMPL if vendor security requirements (SOC 2/ISO evidence, data handling) are collected for each integration provider; PART if for major vendors only; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Which security assurances do you collect from integration vendors?

controls.control: The allowed-actions policy restricts workflows to GitHub, verified creators or an allow-list; third-party action use is governed.
controls.rule: IMPL if allowed_actions = selected with github_owned_allowed = true, verified_allowed = true or an explicit patterns_allowed list (or local_only), on every org (or enforced at enterprise), AND every third-party action used in sampled workflows matches the allow-list; PART if allowed_actions = selected but patterns include wildcards like '*/*' or 1-5 unlisted actions found; NOT if allowed_actions = all.

controls.control: Third-party actions are pinned to a full commit SHA and kept current through Dependabot version updates for the github-actions ecosystem.
controls.rule: For every uses: reference to a non-local, non-GitHub-owned action: pinned = 40-hex SHA. IMPL if >= 95% of third-party action references are SHA-pinned AND >= 80% of repos with workflows have dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem: github-actions; PART if 70-95% pinned; NOT if < 70%. Also report GitHub-owned pinning % separately.

controls.control: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions are read-only, workflows declare least-privilege permissions, and pull requests from forks or first-time contributors require approval to run.
controls.rule: IMPL if default_workflow_permissions = read AND can_approve_pull_request_reviews = false on every org, >= 80% of workflows declare a permissions: block (top-level or on every job), no workflow uses pull_request_target with checkout of the PR head, and fork PR workflows require approval for all outside collaborators (UI); PART if default read but < 80% declare permissions or 1-2 pull_request_target risks; NOT if default write.

controls.control: Shared build and security steps run through reusable or required workflows; workflow files are protected by rulesets and CODEOWNERS.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 active org ruleset uses a 'workflows' rule (required workflows) OR >= 50% of active repos call a reusable workflow from a central repo, AND CODEOWNERS covers .github/workflows on >= 80% of critical repos with code owner review required; PART if reuse 20-50% or CODEOWNERS coverage 50-80%; NOT if neither.

controls.control: Deployment secrets live in environments with required reviewers; long-lived cloud credentials are replaced by OIDC federation.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of production-like environments have required_reviewers, >= 70% of deploying workflows use OIDC (permissions id-token: write + a cloud login action) and production secrets are environment-scoped; PART if reviewers 50-90% or OIDC 30-70%; NOT if production secrets are repo-level with no reviewers or OIDC < 30%.

controls.control: Self-hosted runners are ephemeral or isolated, patched, network-restricted and never shared with public repositories; runner groups control repository access.
controls.rule: IMPL if every self-hosted runner is ephemeral (ephemeral = true or ARC autoscaled), runner groups have allows_public_repositories = false and visibility = selected for sensitive groups, no self-hosted label appears in public repos' workflows, and patching/network isolation is documented; PART if <= 20% persistent runners or one group misconfigured; NOT if persistent shared runners or public-repo exposure.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are self-hosted runners built, patched, isolated and recycled?

controls.control: Build artifacts carry provenance attestations and are stored in governed registries (GitHub Packages) with access control and retention.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 80% of release-producing critical repos generate attestations (actions/attest-build-provenance or verified attestations on release/package digests) and publish to GitHub Packages or a governed registry with access control and retention (interview); PART if 30-80% or registry ungoverned; NOT if < 30%.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Where are build artifacts stored, who can publish and pull, and what is the retention?

controls.control: Production deployments use environment protection rules: required approvals, wait timers and deployment branch policies.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of production-like environments have required_reviewers (>= 1, prevent_self_review = true) AND deployment_branch_policy restricting to protected branches or custom patterns, with wait_timer where policy requires; PART if 70-95%; NOT if < 70% or no production environments defined.

controls.control: Security configurations are defined at organization level (GitHub-recommended or custom) and applied to all repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 organization (or enterprise) security configuration exists with dependency_graph, dependabot_alerts, dependabot_security_updates, code_scanning_default_setup, secret_scanning, secret_scanning_push_protection all enabled and attached/enforced to >= 95% of non-archived repos; PART if configurations exist with 70-95% coverage or missing <= 2 features; NOT if no configuration or coverage < 70%.

controls.control: Security configurations are enforced (repository admins cannot disable) and a default configuration is set for new repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if the primary configuration has enforcement = enforced AND defaults.default_for_new_repos = all (or private_and_internal + public covered); PART if enforced but no default, or default set but unenforced; NOT if neither.

controls.control: Code Security and Secret Protection coverage is measured across all repositories and gaps are tracked to closure.
controls.rule: Coverage per feature (Code Security: dependabot alerts, code scanning; Secret Protection: secret scanning, push protection) = repos with feature enabled / eligible non-archived repos. IMPL if each >= 95% and a gap list with owners exists (interview optional); PART if any 80-95%; NOT if any < 80%.

controls.control: Configuration drift (repositories in 'failed', 'updating' or detached status) is monitored and remediated.
controls.rule: drift = repos with status in (failed, updating > 24h, detached) across configurations. IMPL if drift = 0; PART if drift <= 2% of repos; NOT if > 2%.

controls.control: GitHub Advanced Security licence consumption (active committers) is tracked and forecast against entitlement.
controls.rule: IMPL if purchased_advanced_security_committers >= total_advanced_security_committers with >= 10% headroom AND a forecast/owner exists (interview optional); PART if headroom 0-10%; NOT if total > purchased (over-consumption) or figures unavailable.

controls.control: Secret scanning is enabled on every repository, including internal and private repositories and archived repositories where relevant.
controls.rule: IMPL if secret_scanning enabled on 100% of non-archived repos (public, private, internal) and on archived repos holding recent history (optional); PART if 95-100%; NOT if < 95%.

controls.control: Push protection is enabled and enforced; bypass requires a documented reason and delegated bypass reviewers are configured for sensitive repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if secret_scanning_push_protection enabled on >= 98% of non-archived repos, the configuration is enforced, AND delegated bypass (secret_scanning_delegated_bypass) is enabled with reviewers on critical repos; PART if push protection >= 90% without delegated bypass; NOT if < 90%.

controls.control: Push protection bypass events are monitored, reviewed and followed up.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit action secret_scanning_push_protection.bypass events in 90 days are all matched to a review record (or delegated-bypass request approved) AND a SIEM detection exists for the action; PART if detection exists but reviews incomplete; NOT if bypasses unreviewed and undetected.

controls.control: Custom patterns cover organization-specific secrets (internal tokens, connection strings) and are not used for PII.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 published custom pattern covers organisation-specific secrets (internal tokens, connection strings) with push protection enabled on the pattern and no pattern targets PII; PART if patterns exist unpublished or without push protection; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which internal secret formats exist that GitHub's default patterns do not cover?

controls.control: Validity checks for partner patterns and non-provider (generic) patterns are enabled where appropriate.
controls.rule: IMPL if secret_scanning_validity_checks = enabled and secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns = enabled in the primary configuration (or on >= 95% of repos via security_and_analysis); PART if one of the two; NOT if neither.

controls.control: Secret scanning alerts are triaged with an owner and SLA; leaked credentials are revoked and rotated, not only dismissed.
controls.rule: IMPL if 0 open alerts with validity = active older than 7 days, median time to resolve (180 days) <= 14 days, and >= 70% of resolutions are 'revoked' (vs wont_fix/false_positive); PART if <= 5 active alerts > 7 days or revoked share 40-70%; NOT if > 5 active leaked secrets or revoked share < 40%.

controls.control: The historical alert backlog has been reviewed and reduced to an agreed baseline.
controls.rule: IMPL if open alert count decreased >= 50% over 90 days or is below the agreed baseline (default: <= 1 open alert per 20 repos) with no open alert older than 90 days having validity active; PART if trend flat with backlog triaged (all open alerts have a comment/assignee); NOT if backlog growing.

controls.control: Code scanning is enabled across all supported languages using default setup, with advanced setup only where required.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of eligible repos (CodeQL-supported language) have default setup configured (state = configured) covering all supported languages present, with advanced setup only where a documented reason exists; PART if 80-95%; NOT if < 80%.

controls.control: The CodeQL query suite (default or security-extended) is chosen deliberately and documented per repository class.
controls.rule: IMPL if query_suite is 'extended' for critical repos (or documented decision for 'default') and the choice is documented per repository class; PART if consistent but undocumented; NOT if inconsistent and undocumented.
controls.interview_question: Which CodeQL query suite do you use for critical repositories and why?

controls.control: Code scanning runs on pull requests and high or critical alerts block merge through rulesets (code scanning merge protection).
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of code-scanning-enabled repos have PR analyses (ref refs/pull/*/merge) in 30 days AND an active ruleset code_scanning rule with security_alerts_threshold in (high_or_higher, critical) applies to >= 95% of critical repos; PART if PR scanning >= 60% and gate on 50-95%; NOT otherwise.

controls.control: Code scanning alerts are triaged with severity-based SLAs; dismissal reasons are reviewed and false-positive rates tracked.
controls.rule: IMPL if 0 open critical alerts > 7 days and 0 open high > 30 days, median fix time (180 days) for critical/high <= 30 days, dismissal share <= 30% with 100% of dismissals carrying a reason; PART if <= 10% breach or dismissal share 30-50%; NOT if > 10% breach or dismissal > 50%.

controls.control: Copilot Autofix is enabled for code scanning alerts and its adoption (suggested vs accepted fixes) is measured.
controls.rule: IMPL if Copilot Autofix is enabled at org level (UI) and sampled open alerts return autofix status success/pending for >= 50%, with acceptance tracked (security overview Autofix metrics); PART if enabled but not tracked; NOT if disabled.
controls.interview_question: Is Copilot Autofix enabled, and do you measure how many suggested fixes get merged?

controls.control: Security campaigns are used to drive remediation of alert backlogs, with campaign owners, due dates, templates and progress tracking.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 campaign was created in the last 180 days with managers assigned, ends_at set, and closed_count / total alerts >= 50% at or after due date (or campaign completed); PART if campaigns exist with < 50% progress or no managers/due date; NOT if no campaigns (or feature unavailable — record N/A on GHES without campaigns).

controls.control: Third-party scanner results (SARIF) are consolidated into code scanning where other tools are used, avoiding parallel triage queues.
controls.rule: IMPL if third-party scanners used in workflows (trivy, snyk, sonar, checkov, semgrep, etc.) upload SARIF (upload-sarif step) so that analyses.tool.name lists them, in >= 90% of repos using such tools; PART if 50-90%; NOT if < 50% (parallel triage queues). N/A if no third-party scanner is used.

controls.control: Dependency graph and Dependabot alerts are enabled on all repositories with a supported manifest.
controls.rule: IMPL if dependency_graph and dependabot_alerts are enabled on 100% of non-archived repos with a supported manifest (SBOM returns packages); PART if 90-100%; NOT if < 90%.

controls.control: Dependabot security updates and version updates are configured (dependabot.yml) with grouping and auto-triage rules to keep noise manageable.
controls.rule: IMPL if dependabot_security_updates enabled on >= 95% of eligible repos, >= 80% of eligible repos have dependabot.yml with version updates using groups:, and >= 1 auto-triage rule exists at org level; PART if 60-80% dependabot.yml or no groups; NOT if < 60%.

controls.control: Dependency review runs on pull requests with a severity and licence policy, blocking non-compliant dependencies.
controls.rule: IMPL if actions/dependency-review-action runs on pull_request in >= 90% of eligible repos with fail-on-severity set (<= high) and a licence allow/deny list, and it is a required status check on critical repos; PART if 50-90% or no licence policy; NOT if < 50%.

controls.control: SBOMs can be exported for releases and are consumed by downstream compliance processes.
controls.rule: IMPL if SBOM export works for >= 95% of active repos AND release workflows export/attach an SBOM (anchore/sbom-action, advanced-security/sbom-generator-action or API export) for critical repos, consumed by a downstream process (interview); PART if exportable but not attached/consumed; NOT if dependency graph disabled.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who consumes SBOMs (compliance, customers) and how are they produced at release time?

controls.control: Artifact attestations and build provenance are generated for release artifacts and verified before deployment.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 80% of critical release-producing repos use actions/attest-build-provenance (or sigstore/cosign attest) AND a sampled artifact passes gh attestation verify, AND deployment workflows verify attestations before deploy (gh attestation verify step) in >= 50%; PART if attestations generated but not verified; NOT if none.

controls.control: Actions supply chain is hardened: allowed-actions policy, third-party actions pinned to a commit SHA, GITHUB_TOKEN read-only by default and OIDC used for cloud credentials.
controls.rule: Composite of SEC-098/018/019/021: IMPL if allowed_actions != all, third-party SHA-pinned >= 95%, default_workflow_permissions = read, and OIDC used by >= 70% of deploying workflows; PART if 3 of 4; NOT if <= 2.

controls.control: Security overview dashboards (risk, coverage, alert trends, mean time to remediate) are reviewed on a defined cadence.
controls.rule: IMPL if security overview (risk, coverage, trends, MTTR) is reviewed on a defined cadence (at least monthly) by named roles with minutes/actions; PART if reviewed ad hoc; NOT if never.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who reviews the security overview dashboards, how often, and what decisions come out of it?

controls.control: The security manager role (or custom organization roles) gives the security team least-privilege access instead of organization ownership.
controls.rule: IMPL if the security team is assigned security_manager (team) or a custom org role with security permissions and no security team member is an org owner solely for security work; PART if security_manager assigned but some security staff are owners; NOT if security access is through owner only.

controls.control: Alert ownership is defined (teams or CODEOWNERS mapped to repositories) and remediation SLAs per severity are documented and measured.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of critical repos have CODEOWNERS or a team with maintain/admin (ownership mapping) AND an SLA policy per severity is documented and measured (report); PART if ownership >= 80% but SLA undocumented; NOT if ownership < 80%.
controls.interview_question: Show the remediation SLA policy per severity and the latest adherence report.

controls.control: Security alert and audit events feed the SIEM (webhooks or audit log streaming) with detections for push protection bypasses, alert dismissals and configuration changes.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log streaming is active AND webhooks/Apps deliver code_scanning_alert, secret_scanning_alert, dependabot_alert, repository_ruleset and secret_scanning_alert_location events to the SIEM, AND detections exist for push-protection bypass, alert dismissal and configuration change; PART if streaming + <= 1 detection; NOT if none.

controls.control: GitHub security capabilities are mapped to the organization's Secure SDLC controls and control owners, with gaps identified.
controls.rule: IMPL if a mapping document links each Secure SDLC control to GitHub capabilities and named control owners with identified gaps; PART if partial mapping; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Show how your Secure SDLC controls map to GitHub features and who owns each control.

controls.control: Required security gates (code review, code scanning, dependency review, secret scanning) are defined per repository class and enforced through rulesets and required workflows.
controls.rule: IMPL if repository classes exist (custom property) and each class has an active ruleset enforcing its gates (critical: >= 2 reviews + code owner review + required checks incl. code scanning gate + dependency review + signatures; standard: >= 1 review + required checks), with >= 95% of repos matching their class ruleset; PART if gates defined without class targeting (one-size) or 80-95%; NOT if < 80%.

controls.control: Approval requirements for production changes are implemented through environment approvals and required reviewers, and evidenced.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of production environments require reviewers with prevent_self_review, default-branch PR review is required, and sampled production deployments (90 days) each show an approval record (deployment protection rule review); PART if 70-95%; NOT if < 70%.

controls.control: Evidence for audits is collected automatically where possible (rule evaluation history, workflow run logs, alert history).
controls.rule: IMPL if evidence collection is automated: rule-suites (ruleset insights) exported >= monthly, workflow run logs archived beyond 90 days, alert history exported (API/overview CSV) into an evidence store; PART if 1-2 automated; NOT if manual screenshots only.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which audit evidence is collected automatically today, and where does it land?

controls.control: Exception handling and risk acceptance follow a documented process with owner and expiry, tracked in a register.
controls.rule: IMPL if exceptions/risk acceptances follow a documented process with owner, approver and expiry, tracked in a register with no expired items open; PART if register exists with expired items or no expiry; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Show the exception and risk-acceptance register for GitHub controls.

controls.control: Ensure teams are well-versed in the intent of branch rules and verify rules are in place.
controls.rule: Data: active org rulesets targeting default branches (~DEFAULT_BRANCH include), % active repos with effective default-branch protection. IMPL if >= 90% of active repos are protected AND teams can explain the intent of the rules (interview); PART if 60-90%; NOT if < 60%.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Do teams understand why branch rules exist and how to request changes? Who owns the rulesets?

controls.control: Leverage pull requests and enforce branch rules to maintain code quality.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of active repos require pull requests on the default branch and >= 90% of default-branch commits in the sample come through PRs; PART if 60-90%; NOT if < 60%.

controls.control: Verify that required status checks are enabled.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 80% of active repos with CI have required_status_checks (>= 1 context) with strict_required_status_checks_policy = true on the default branch; PART if 50-80% or non-strict; NOT if < 50%.

controls.control: Ensure code review requirements are set.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of active repos require >= 1 approving review (>= 2 for critical repos) with dismiss_stale_reviews_on_push and require_last_push_approval enabled for critical repos; PART if 60-90% require reviews; NOT if < 60%.

controls.control: Review compliance checks for code and dependencies.
controls.rule: IMPL if dependency review (actions/dependency-review-action) or an equivalent policy check runs on PRs in >= 80% of eligible repos AND is required (status check or required workflow) on critical repos; PART if 40-80%; NOT if < 40%.

controls.control: Ensure automated tools are integrated for continuous compliance.
controls.rule: IMPL if compliance is continuous: >= 1 org ruleset with a 'workflows' (required workflow) or 'code_scanning' rule targeting default branches AND an enforced security configuration; PART if one of the two; NOT if none.

controls.control: Check the usage and monitoring of GitHub audit logs for governance.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log is accessible to the governance team and streamed; PART if accessible only; NOT if not accessible/used.

controls.control: Ensure audit logs are retained for an appropriate period, depending on usage of GitHub Enterprise Cloud/Server or another business application.
controls.rule: GHEC retains 180 days (Git events 7 days): IMPL if streaming to storage with retention >= the customer's requirement (default 365 days, evidenced by destination retention policy); PART if streamed with unknown retention; NOT if not streamed and requirement > 180 days. GHES: IMPL if log forwarding is enabled to a store with >= required retention.

controls.control: Regularly review audit logs for unusual activities.
controls.rule: IMPL if reviews/detections run at least weekly with outcomes recorded; PART if monthly; NOT if never.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How often does someone look at GitHub audit events, and what was the last anomaly found?

controls.control: Ensure all modifications to documents and code are tracked using version control.
controls.rule: IMPL if documentation and infrastructure-as-code live in repositories (docs repo exists; IaC files found in >= 1 repo) and those repos require PRs on the default branch; PART if in repos without PR requirement; NOT if docs/config are managed outside version control (interview).

controls.control: Verify that version control policies are enforced.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of active repos have effective rules blocking force pushes (non_fast_forward) and deletions on the default branch, and rulesets are in 'active' enforcement (not 'evaluate') with bypass_actors limited to <= 2 roles/teams; PART if 60-90% or rulesets in evaluate mode; NOT if < 60%.

controls.control: Implement continuous logging for all critical resources within the environment.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log streaming (GHEC) or syslog forwarding (GHES) is enabled AND Actions/security events reach a log platform (webhooks or streaming); PART if audit only; NOT if none.

controls.control: Ensure logs are securely stored and accessible for audits.
controls.rule: IMPL if the log store has RBAC limited to security/audit staff, retention >= requirement and immutability; PART if RBAC without retention/immutability; NOT if store is open or unknown.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who can access GitHub logs in the destination store, and how long are they kept?

controls.control: Utilize custom properties to manage and categorize repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 2 custom properties are defined (e.g. criticality, data_classification, owner/team) and >= 1 is required; PART if 1 property or none required; NOT if no schema.

controls.control: Ensure custom properties are consistently applied across repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of non-archived repos have a non-null value for every required property (or for the criticality property when none is required); PART if 70-95%; NOT if < 70%.

controls.control: Regularly review and update custom properties to reflect organizational needs.
controls.rule: Data: properties referenced by ruleset conditions (repository_property) and configurations. IMPL if properties drive automation (>= 1 ruleset uses repository_property) and are reviewed at least annually; PART if defined but unused in rules; NOT if never reviewed and unused.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who owns the custom property schema, and how are values kept accurate as repositories change?

controls.control: Assess the implementation of role-based access control for repository and organization access.
controls.rule: IMPL if team-based access >= 90%, owners <= 5 (or <= 5% of members), security team via security_manager/custom role, and custom repository roles used where needed; PART if team-based 70-90% or owners 6-10; NOT if team-based < 70% or owners > 10.

controls.control: Ensure roles are clearly defined and documented.
controls.rule: IMPL if a roles matrix documents each GitHub role (owner, member, security manager, custom roles, repo roles) with who may hold it and matches the assignments in org.roles; PART if matrix exists but diverges (> 10% unexplained assignments); NOT if no matrix.
controls.interview_question: Show the document defining GitHub roles and who is allowed to hold each.

controls.control: Create a process for requesting and granting access, and have the timestamps of access requests available.
controls.rule: Data: audit events org.add_member, team.add_member, repo.add_member with timestamps; PAT requests with created_at/approval. IMPL if access is requested through a ticketed workflow and >= 90% of sampled grants (last 90 days) map to a request with timestamps; PART if 50-90%; NOT if grants are ad hoc.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How does someone request access to GitHub or a repository, and where is the request/approval recorded?

controls.control: Clearly define and document each role's access rights and responsibilities.
controls.rule: IMPL if access rights documentation (who has what and why) is current (reviewed <= 12 months) and matches the exported membership; PART if exists but stale; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Provide the current access rights documentation for GitHub and its last review date.

controls.control: Regularly review and update access rights documentation.
controls.rule: IMPL if access rights documentation (who has what and why) is current (reviewed <= 12 months) and matches the exported membership; PART if exists but stale; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Provide the current access rights documentation for GitHub and its last review date.

controls.control: Regularly monitor user activities to ensure compliance with access policies.
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log is streamed and detections cover both administrative (org.*, business.*, team.*) and repository (repo.access, repo.destroy, protected_branch.*, repository_ruleset.*) actions; PART if streamed with only one category covered; NOT if not streamed.

controls.control: Implement alerts for suspicious activities at both the administrative and repository level.
controls.rule: IMPL if alert rules exist for >= 3 administrative actions and >= 3 repository actions with notification routing; PART if >= 1 in each; NOT if none.

controls.control: Establish and test incident response procedures for unauthorized access or policy violations.
controls.rule: IMPL if GitHub incident scenarios are in the IR plan with named roles and were exercised in 12 months; PART if documented without exercise; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which GitHub incident scenarios does your response plan cover, and when were they last exercised?

controls.control: Ensure incident response plans are documented and accessible.
controls.rule: IMPL if GitHub incident scenarios are in the IR plan with named roles and were exercised in 12 months; PART if documented without exercise; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which GitHub incident scenarios does your response plan cover, and when were they last exercised?

controls.control: Ensure governance policies are regularly reviewed and updated to adapt to new requirements.

controls.control: Involve stakeholders in the policy update process, such as application owners and change managers.

controls.rule: IMPL if quarterly access reviews (members, owners, outside collaborators, teams, apps) are recorded with removals; PART if semi-annual/annual; NOT if none.

controls.control: Implement configuration management practices to maintain consistency and control over the environment.

controls.control: Regularly perform compliance audits to ensure adherence to governance policies and regulatory requirements.
controls.rule: IMPL if GitHub is in scope of internal/external compliance audits with findings tracked; PART if audited without tracking; NOT if out of scope.
controls.interview_question: Is GitHub in scope of your compliance audits? Share the last findings.

controls.control: Document and address any findings from compliance audits.
controls.rule: IMPL if GitHub is in scope of internal/external compliance audits with findings tracked; PART if audited without tracking; NOT if out of scope.
controls.interview_question: Is GitHub in scope of your compliance audits? Share the last findings.

controls.control: Review and configure GitHub Enterprise settings to align with organizational governance policies.
controls.rule: IMPL if enterprise policies ENFORCE (not NO_POLICY) for: repository creation, visibility change, deletion, forking, default permission, 2FA, Actions allowed actions and workflow permissions; PART if >= 5 of 8 enforced; NOT if < 5 (organizations decide).

controls.control: Ensure settings are documented and regularly reviewed.
controls.rule: IMPL if a settings baseline document lists every enterprise/org setting with its intended value and matches the collected values (>= 95%); PART if document exists with < 95% match or no review in 12 months; NOT if none.
