controls.control: Ensure high availability and disaster recovery plans are in place for GitHub Enterprise Server.
controls.rule: GHES only. IMPL if replication status is OK for all services (ghe-repl-status), a replica exists in a separate failure domain, and a DR plan with RTO/RPO exists; PART if HA configured without DR plan, or WARN states; NOT if no replica.
controls.interview_question: Show the DR plan for GHES (RTO/RPO, failover steps) and the replica topology.

controls.control: Regularly test high availability and disaster recovery plans.
controls.rule: GHES only. IMPL if failover/DR is tested at least annually with recorded results; PART if tested > 12 months ago; NOT if never.
controls.interview_question: When was the last GHES failover test and what did you learn?

controls.control: Integrate GitHub Enterprise with existing security tools and frameworks (e.g., SSO, SCIM).
controls.rule: IMPL if SSO configured, SCIM/EMU provisioning active, audit log streaming active, and >= 1 security tooling App installed (SIEM connector or security scanner); PART if 2-3 of 4; NOT if <= 1.

controls.control: Regularly review and update security integrations.
controls.rule: Data: installed security Apps with updated_at age, stream configuration updated_at, SAML certificate expiry (UI). IMPL if security integrations (SSO, SCIM, SIEM streaming, scanners) have named owners and were reviewed within 12 months (records) and no integration shows a stale state (suspended App, paused stream, certificate < 30 days to expiry); PART if reviewed ad hoc or one stale state; NOT if never reviewed.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Who owns each security integration with GitHub and when was it last reviewed?

controls.control: Implement performance monitoring to ensure the GitHub Enterprise environment is running efficiently.
controls.rule: GHES: IMPL if collectd/SNMP or an external monitoring agent collects appliance metrics with dashboards; GHEC: IMPL if Actions performance metrics (queue time, run duration) are reviewed monthly; PART if metrics exist without review; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which dashboards show GitHub platform performance (GHES appliance or Actions performance metrics), and who reviews them?

controls.control: Regularly review performance metrics and address any issues.
controls.rule: IMPL if performance issues are tracked to resolution with examples in 12 months; PART if reactive only; NOT if not tracked.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Describe a recent performance issue on GitHub and how it was resolved.

controls.control: Ensure data residency requirements are met for GitHub Enterprise deployments.
controls.rule: IMPL if data residency requirements are documented and satisfied by the deployment with evidence; PART if known without evidence; NOT if unknown.
controls.interview_question: Which data residency constraints apply to GitHub data, and how are they satisfied?

controls.control: Document and regularly review data residency policies.
controls.rule: IMPL if data residency requirements are documented and satisfied by the deployment with evidence; PART if known without evidence; NOT if unknown.
controls.interview_question: Which data residency constraints apply to GitHub data, and how are they satisfied?

controls.control: Develop and enforce custom policies specific to the organization's use of GitHub Enterprise.
controls.rule: IMPL if custom governance policies (naming, repo lifecycle, exceptions) are documented, approved and enforced through rulesets/properties; PART if documented only; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Which organisation-specific GitHub policies exist beyond vendor defaults, and how are they enforced?

controls.control: Regularly review and update custom policies.
controls.rule: IMPL if custom governance policies (naming, repo lifecycle, exceptions) are documented, approved and enforced through rulesets/properties; PART if documented only; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Which organisation-specific GitHub policies exist beyond vendor defaults, and how are they enforced?

controls.control: Automate user provisioning and de-provisioning to maintain control over access.
controls.rule: Same as SEC-080: IMPL if SCIM/EMU/LDAP sync active with >= 95% coverage; PART if 80-95%; NOT if none.

controls.control: Regularly review and update user provisioning processes.
controls.rule: Data: SCIM users lastModified distribution, IdP-group-synced teams (team sync), audit team.* events. IMPL if provisioning rules (IdP group to team/role mapping) are documented and reviewed within 12 months and >= 90% of teams are IdP-synced (or membership changes are all SCIM/automation-driven in the audit log); PART if documented without review or 50-90% synced; NOT if manual membership management with no review.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are IdP group-to-GitHub team mappings maintained and reviewed?

controls.control: Establish a support and maintenance plan for GitHub Enterprise, including regular updates and patches for Server, or communication of features for both Cloud and Server.
controls.rule: IMPL if a support model (GitHub Premium/Enterprise support, internal L1/L2, maintenance windows) is documented and used; PART if informal; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How is GitHub supported internally, and how do you engage GitHub Support?

controls.control: Ensure support and maintenance plans are documented and accessible.
controls.rule: IMPL if a support model (GitHub Premium/Enterprise support, internal L1/L2, maintenance windows) is documented and used; PART if informal; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How is GitHub supported internally, and how do you engage GitHub Support?

controls.control: SAML SSO (or Enterprise Managed Users) with Entra ID is enforced for the enterprise; SSO recovery codes and emergency-access accounts are documented and tested.
controls.rule: IMPL if SAML/OIDC SSO or EMU is enforced for the enterprise (every org), the IdP is Entra ID (issuer contains login.microsoftonline.com/sts.windows.net) or the approved IdP, AND recovery codes/emergency access accounts are documented with custody and tested in 12 months; PART if SSO enforced but recovery undocumented; NOT if SSO not enforced.
controls.interview_question: Who holds the SSO recovery codes and emergency-access account credentials, and when was recovery last tested?

controls.control: SCIM provisioning and de-provisioning is active and joiner, mover and leaver events are reflected in GitHub within an agreed SLA.
controls.rule: IMPL if SCIM (or EMU) provisioning is active with coverage >= 95% of members AND sampled leaver events (IdP deactivation) are followed by org.remove_member / user suspension within 24h in the audit log; PART if coverage 80-95% or removal within 7 days; NOT if no SCIM or removals > 7 days.

controls.control: Two-factor authentication is required for all members and outside collaborators; unenrolled users are tracked to zero.
controls.rule: IMPL if two_factor_requirement_enabled = true on every org (or enterprise twoFactorRequiredSetting = ENABLED) AND members with 2FA disabled = 0 AND outside collaborators with 2FA disabled = 0; PART if requirement on but 1-5 unenrolled users tracked; NOT if requirement off or > 5.

controls.control: Enterprise and organization owners are minimised, named and reviewed; segregation of duties between platform administration and security is defined.
controls.rule: IMPL if enterprise owners <= 3 and org owners <= max(2, 5% of members) and <= 5, all owners are named individuals (no shared accounts), and a segregation-of-duties statement separates platform admins from security reviewers; PART if counts within limits but no SoD statement, or counts exceed by <= 2; NOT if owners exceed limits by > 2 or shared accounts exist.
controls.interview_question: Who are the enterprise and organization owners, why does each need it, and how are platform administration and security review separated?

controls.control: Custom organization roles and custom repository roles implement least privilege for platform, security and developer personas.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 custom organization role or the security_manager role is assigned to the security team AND >= 1 custom repository role exists where base roles are insufficient (or interview confirms base roles suffice), AND no team holds org owner for convenience; PART if security_manager used but no custom roles evaluated; NOT if all privileged access is via owner.

controls.control: Personal access tokens are governed: fine-grained tokens preferred, classic tokens restricted, approval workflow and maximum lifetime enforced.
controls.rule: IMPL if fine-grained PATs: allowed with approval required; classic PATs: restricted; maximum lifetime set (<= 366 days fine-grained, <= 366 days classic if allowed); no pending requests older than 7 days; PART if approval required but classic allowed or no max lifetime; NOT if unrestricted.

controls.control: Service accounts, deploy keys, SSH keys, GitHub Apps and OAuth apps are inventoried, owned, least-scoped and rotated; OAuth app access restrictions are enabled.
controls.rule: Data: GitHub Apps (permissions), deploy keys (read_only, age), approved OAuth apps, fine-grained PAT grants. IMPL if OAuth restrictions enabled, every App/deploy key/service account appears in a customer registry with owner (>= 95%), deploy keys are read_only unless justified and < 365 days old, and no App has administration:write without justification; PART if registry covers 70-95%; NOT if no registry or OAuth restrictions off.
controls.interview_question: Show the inventory of service accounts, deploy keys, GitHub Apps and OAuth apps with owners and rotation dates.

controls.control: Outside collaborators are limited and justified, and periodic access reviews for members, teams and collaborators are evidenced.
controls.rule: IMPL if outside collaborators < 5% of members, each with a justification in a register, and access reviews (members, teams, collaborators) are evidenced quarterly; PART if collaborators 5-10% or reviews semi-annual; NOT if > 10% or no reviews.
controls.interview_question: Why does each outside collaborator have access, and when was the last access review?

controls.control: The enterprise > organization > repository policy hierarchy is documented and enterprise policies lock the settings that must not vary between organizations.
controls.rule: IMPL if a policy hierarchy document exists AND enterprise policies enforce (not NO_POLICY) the settings marked 'must not vary' in that document (at minimum: 2FA, repo creation/visibility/deletion/forking, default permission, allowed actions, workflow permissions, Copilot policies); PART if document exists with <= 2 unenforced items or enforcement without document; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Which settings must be identical across organizations, and where is that written down?

controls.control: Organization design and administrative boundaries are deliberate (by business unit or environment) and avoid fragmented organizations.
controls.rule: Data: organization count, repos per org, members per org. IMPL if org design follows a documented rationale (by business unit/environment) with <= 1 org per 50 repos on average or a justified exception, and no orgs with < 3 repos older than 12 months (unless sandbox); PART if rationale exists but fragmentation (many tiny orgs); NOT if no rationale.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Why are organizations structured as they are, and who may create a new one?

controls.control: Repository creation, visibility changes, transfers, deletion and forking are restricted to appropriate roles; inactive repositories are archived.
controls.rule: IMPL if members_can_create_public_repositories = false, members_can_create_repositories = false or restricted to private/internal, members_can_fork_private_repositories = false, enterprise policies for visibility change and deletion = DISABLED for members, AND stale repos (no push 365 days, not archived) <= 10%; PART if 1 setting open or stale 10-25%; NOT if >= 2 settings open or stale > 25%.

controls.control: Repositories are classified by criticality and data sensitivity with custom properties, and rulesets target repositories by those properties.
controls.rule: IMPL if custom properties include a criticality/tier AND a data classification property, coverage >= 95% of non-archived repos, and >= 1 active ruleset uses a repository_property condition on those values; PART if properties exist with 70-95% coverage or no ruleset targeting; NOT if no classification properties.

controls.control: Organization rulesets require pull request reviews and status checks on default branches and block force pushes and deletions.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 active org ruleset targets ~DEFAULT_BRANCH across all/most repos AND effective default-branch rules on >= 95% of active repos include pull_request (>= 1 approval), required_status_checks (>= 1 context), non_fast_forward (block force push) and deletion; PART if 80-95% or missing one rule type; NOT if < 80%.

controls.control: CODEOWNERS files exist on critical repositories and code owner review is required by rulesets.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 95% of critical repos have a CODEOWNERS file with 0 errors (codeowners/errors) AND effective rules set require_code_owner_review = true on their default branch, AND CODEOWNERS covers .github/workflows; PART if 70-95% or code owner review not required; NOT if < 70%.

controls.control: Signed (verified) commits are required on protected branches of critical repositories.
controls.rule: IMPL if required_signatures is in the effective default-branch rules for >= 95% of critical repos AND >= 95% of the last 100 default-branch commits on those repos are verified; PART if rule present on 50-95% or verified ratio 80-95%; NOT if < 50% (web_commit_signoff_required alone does not count).

controls.control: Ruleset bypass actors are minimised and bypass usage is monitored; security exceptions and configuration drift are tracked with owner and expiry.
controls.rule: Data: bypass_actors per ruleset (count, types), rule-suites with result=bypass in 30 days, audit protected_branch.policy_override events, exception register. IMPL if every active ruleset has <= 2 bypass actors (no 'RepositoryRole: admin' always-bypass on critical repos), bypass events are reviewed (evidence) and an exception register with owner+expiry exists; PART if bypass actors <= 4 and register exists; NOT if broad bypass or no register.
controls.interview_question: Who can bypass rulesets and why, and where are approved exceptions recorded with owner and expiry?

controls.control: Enterprise and organization Copilot policies are set deliberately for each surface (chat, coding agent, code review, CLI, models) and documented.
controls.rule: IMPL if every Copilot policy surface (IDE/chat, GitHub.com chat, CLI, coding agent, code review, MCP servers, extensions, custom instructions, models/preview features) has an explicit value (no 'No policy' left to orgs unless documented) at enterprise level, and the decisions are documented; PART if <= 2 surfaces unset or undocumented; NOT if unset.
controls.interview_question: Which Copilot features are allowed for which populations, and where is that decision recorded?

controls.control: Suggestions matching public code are blocked or the decision is documented; content exclusion protects sensitive repositories and paths.
controls.rule: IMPL if public_code_suggestions = block (or a documented risk acceptance for allow) AND content exclusion rules exist covering repositories/paths classified sensitive (>= 1 rule, aligned to the classification property); PART if block set without content exclusion or vice versa; NOT if allow with no documentation and no exclusions.

controls.control: MCP servers, Copilot extensions, plugins and marketplace apps are governed by an allow-list and approval process with named owners.
controls.rule: IMPL if MCP servers and Copilot extensions are restricted to an allow-list (policy set to allow-list/disabled with approved list) with named owners and an approval record per item; PART if enabled broadly with a registry; NOT if enabled with no governance.
controls.interview_question: Which MCP servers and Copilot extensions are approved, who owns each, and how are new ones approved?

controls.control: Repository custom instructions and custom agents are version-controlled and reviewed, and encode security requirements for generated code.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 80% of critical repos have .github/copilot-instructions.md (or .github/instructions/*.instructions.md / .github/agents/*) under version control, on a protected default branch, mentioning security or testing requirements (keywords: security, secret, input validation, test); PART if 40-80% or files without security content; NOT if < 40%.

controls.control: The Copilot coding agent is enabled only for approved repositories, works on branches protected by rulesets and requires human review before merge.
controls.rule: IMPL if coding agent policy is enabled only for selected repositories (or disabled), 100% of PRs authored by the Copilot agent (author login Copilot / copilot-swe-agent) target repos with PR review required and none were merged without a human approval; PART if enabled for all repos but all agent PRs were human-approved; NOT if agent PRs merged without review or policy unset.

controls.control: Copilot administration, agent and integration events are audited and monitored (audit log copilot.* events streamed to the SIEM).
controls.rule: IMPL if audit log contains copilot.* events (policy changes, seat assignments, coding agent) and streaming is active with >= 1 SIEM detection on copilot policy changes; PART if events present and streamed without detection; NOT if not streamed.

controls.control: A Copilot secure-use standard defines human review, validation of AI-generated code (tests, scanning) and developer responsibilities, backed by training.
controls.rule: IMPL if a Copilot secure-use standard (human review, testing/scanning of AI-generated code, prohibited inputs, responsibilities) exists, is approved and training completion >= 80% of Copilot seat holders; PART if standard without training; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Show the Copilot secure-use standard and training completion for seat holders.

controls.control: New Copilot models, agents, features and integrations go through a security review and approval process with a risk assessment.
controls.rule: IMPL if new Copilot models/agents/features/integrations go through a documented approval with an AI risk assessment (records for the last 3 changes); PART if approvals without risk assessment; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: How were the last Copilot feature or model enablements approved, and is there an AI risk assessment template?

controls.control: Audit log retention meets requirements and audit log streaming (including Git events where needed) is configured to the SIEM or storage.
controls.rule: IMPL if streaming is configured (not paused) to the SIEM/storage, Git events streaming enabled where required, destination retention >= 365 days (or policy requirement), and the audit log API is accessible; PART if streaming without Git events or unknown retention; NOT if no streaming.

controls.control: Detections exist for privileged changes (owner and role changes, policy changes), repository events (visibility change, transfer, deletion), credential events (tokens, deploy keys), workflow and runner changes, push protection bypasses and Copilot policy changes.
controls.rule: Map SIEM rules to required actions: org.add_member/org.update_member/org.remove_member; business.add_admin/business.remove_admin; org.update_default_repository_permission; repo.change_visibility (repo.access)/repo.transfer/repo.destroy; personal_access_token.request_created/access_granted; oauth_application.create; secret_scanning_push_protection.bypass; protected_branch.policy_override/repository_ruleset.update; workflows.* (approve_workflow_job, reject); org.update_actions_secret; copilot.* policy changes. IMPL if >= 90% of these action families have a detection; PART if 50-90%; NOT if < 50%.

controls.control: Security alerts and audit detections have named owners, triage cadence and response SLAs.
controls.rule: IMPL if an ownership matrix names owners for security alerts and audit detections with triage cadence and SLAs (on-call documented); PART if owners without SLAs; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Who owns GitHub security alerts and audit detections, and what are the response SLAs?

controls.control: Playbooks exist and are exercised for leaked credentials, compromised repository or administrator, malicious workflow or runner compromise, and Copilot integration misuse.
controls.rule: IMPL if playbooks exist for leaked credential, compromised repository/administrator, malicious workflow or runner compromise, and Copilot misuse, each exercised in 12 months; PART if >= 2 playbooks or unexercised; NOT if none.
controls.interview_question: Show the GitHub incident playbooks and the last exercise record for each.

controls.control: Audit and security evidence is retained and retrievable for compliance audits (rulesets history, workflow logs, alert history).
controls.rule: IMPL if evidence (rule evaluation history, workflow logs, alert history, audit exports) is retained >= the audit requirement in a system of record and was produced for the last audit; PART if retained but never produced; NOT if not retained beyond GitHub defaults (rule-suites 30 days, workflow logs 90 days).
controls.interview_question: How do you retain GitHub evidence beyond default retention (workflow logs 90 days, rule insights 30 days) for audits?

controls.control: GitHub service health, security advisories and platform dependency alerts are monitored with a defined response.
controls.rule: IMPL if githubstatus.com subscription exists (email/Slack/webhook), GHES release notes/security advisories are tracked with an upgrade cadence (<= 1 release behind), and platform tooling repos (runners, ARC, backup-utils) have Dependabot alerts enabled; PART if 2 of 3; NOT if <= 1.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How do you learn about GitHub incidents, security advisories and new GHES releases?

controls.control: Assess the organization and structure of repositories for clarity and scalability.
controls.rule: Compute: repos total, archived %, forks %, repos without a team (no team permission) %, empty repos (size = 0) %, repos not pushed in 365 days and not archived %. IMPL if stale-unarchived <= 10%, orphan (no team) <= 10%, empty <= 5%; PART if any metric up to 2x threshold; NOT if beyond.

controls.control: Determine whether repositories follow a naming convention, and ensure all repositories have a description.
controls.rule: Infer naming convention: >= 80% of active repo names match one dominant pattern (kebab-case with a team/product prefix, e.g. ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)+$) — record the regex. IMPL if pattern conformance >= 80% AND >= 90% of active repos have a non-empty description; PART if conformance 60-80% or description 70-90%; NOT if below.

controls.control: Check for the use of custom properties to dynamically manage and enforce.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 1 custom property exists with >= 90% coverage and >= 1 ruleset condition uses repository_property; PART if properties exist without ruleset usage; NOT if no properties.

controls.control: Verify that repositories are appropriately segmented so as to avoid monolithic structures unnecessarily, or determine the necessity of such an architecture.
controls.rule: Data: repos > 1 GB (size in KB > 1,048,576), repos with > 50,000 files (tree), repos with >= 3 top-level service directories and multiple manifests (monorepo signal). IMPL if monorepos are deliberate (interview) and have CODEOWNERS per directory + path-filtered workflows; PART if large repos exist without path-based ownership; NOT if unmanaged monoliths cause slow CI (median CI > 30 min).
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: Which repositories are intentionally monorepos, and how do you manage ownership and CI inside them?

controls.control: Check for the use of branch protection rules to maintain code quality.
controls.rule: IMPL if >= 90% of active repos have effective default-branch protection (PR required + block force push); PART if 60-90%; NOT if < 60%.

controls.control: Evaluate the modularity of the codebase for maintainability and scalability.
controls.rule: IMPL if module boundaries are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md or design docs in >= 50% of critical repos) and dependency direction is enforced (lint rules, package boundaries); PART if documented in some; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are module boundaries defined and enforced in your main codebases?

controls.control: Ensure that code modules are reusable and loosely coupled.
controls.rule: IMPL if module boundaries are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md or design docs in >= 50% of critical repos) and dependency direction is enforced (lint rules, package boundaries); PART if documented in some; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are module boundaries defined and enforced in your main codebases?

controls.control: Promote usage of design patterns that promote modularity.
controls.rule: IMPL if module boundaries are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md or design docs in >= 50% of critical repos) and dependency direction is enforced (lint rules, package boundaries); PART if documented in some; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are module boundaries defined and enforced in your main codebases?

controls.control: Verify that dependencies between modules are well-documented.
controls.rule: IMPL if module boundaries are documented (ARCHITECTURE.md or design docs in >= 50% of critical repos) and dependency direction is enforced (lint rules, package boundaries); PART if documented in some; NOT if none.
evidence: interviews/{control-id}.md (or the Controls sheet Finding column)
controls.interview_question: How are module boundaries defined and enforced in your main codebases?

controls.control: Review the consistency of the technology stack across projects for efficiency and interoperability.
controls.rule: Compute the distribution of primary languages and of build tools/frameworks (from SBOM package managers: npm, maven, nuget, pip, go). IMPL if the top 3 languages cover >= 80% of active repos and each language has a dominant package manager (>= 80%); PART if top 3 cover 60-80%; NOT if < 60% (fragmented stack).

controls.control: Ensure that the tech stack is standardized to reduce complexity.
controls.rule: IMPL if a technology radar/approved stack list exists and >= 90% of active repos use approved languages/frameworks; PART if list exists with 70-90% conformance; NOT if no list.
controls.interview_question: Is there an approved technology list or radar? How are exceptions handled?
